# Keep the scene. Send the changes.

45-second voiceover and shot plan. Optional narration only; no audio has been generated. The original 8-second GIF/MP4 is a silent explanatory animation, not paper output.

0–7 seconds — Show the scene and the two update lanes.
Voiceover: “ResStreamGS, an October 15 paper, asks which Gaussian splats actually need refreshing. Here's a synthetic scene that makes the decision visible.”
On-screen: “Keep the scene. Send the changes.” / “Analytic teaching scene”

7–16 seconds — Enable the panel's color changes. Switch to position-only ranking with a tight budget; scrub forward within the group.
Voiceover: “This panel doesn't move, but its color changes. Watch what happens when the update budget only follows position.”
On-screen: “Stationary can still change.”

16–25 seconds — Switch to position plus color, keeping frame, budget and camera fixed. Highlight selected update splats.
Voiceover: “Now let color count too. The same budget goes to different splats. We know this toy scene's trajectories; a real system has to estimate what's important.”
On-screen: “Same budget. Different selection.”

25–34 seconds — Highlight the stable frame and cached lane. Increase the frame-group length.
Voiceover: “The cached frame stays in the picture. Reusing a splat doesn't remove it from rendering. Longer groups share the initial state across more frames, but it can get stale.”
On-screen: “Cached splats still render.”

34–45 seconds — Rotate camera, show pixel RMSE and record counter, then end on the lab URL.
Voiceover: “Turn the camera and the visible error changes. This counter measures update records, not compressed bytes. Try the controls, then export the comparison that explains your point.”
On-screen: “Records ≠ codec bytes” / “120 × 80 pixel error”

Link: https://kavehkamali.github.io/frontier-fieldnotes/stream.html
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21121v1

For an 8-second silent loop: use the changing panel, one fixed camera and one fixed update budget; play the complete scene timeline. Keep the reference/reused labels and analytic-scene caption visible. A longer narrated version can cut between separately exported settings. Don't imply the paper's trained selector is running.
